pages.text: You are small, and slow, and have no fangs worth showing. You can still be alarming.$(br2)Press $(k:hominin_evolution.threat_display) twice - or, with nothing in your hands, $(k:sneak) and $(k:use) at the air: call, and leap, and look bigger than you are.

With a branch or a stone in hand, the same gesture throws it. Something that hurts from a distance is a far better argument than noise.$(br2)Go and pick it up again afterwards. Good stones are not so easy to come by.

A $(l)hammerstone$() throws harder than any cobble - hard, aimed, from an arm built for it. To the head, an aimed one staggers what it hits and can concuss it; a skull already rung can start to bleed. A heave in a display only stings.$(br2)Stone that dense does not always survive the landing: now and then it $(l)shatters$(). Only chert breaks clean enough to leave a flake.

From erectus on, weapons make a display. A weapon in your hand, and every one of your band near you carrying one: each makes whatever you are facing likelier to leave.$(br2)Hunters come one at a time, and go for whoever has strayed from the band - a crowd is left alone. Keep together.

Choose how the band meets what comes for it (Danger): $(l)stand together$(), $(l)overwhelm$() it all at once, keep off and $(l)throw$() with two guarding, or $(l)ambush$() - still, then everything at once. Every band has its own way; ask them, or fight them, or ask a band that knows them. And a hunt can be $(l)kinetic$(): throw first, close after.
